items.fullText: 핫픽! 미국주식 핫픽! 미국주식 브로드컴 매수 상향…팔란티어 목표가 260달러[월가 업&다운] 입력 2026.10.27 22:11 수정 2026.10.27 22:11 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 황정수 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. AI 기사요약 미국 주요 증권사들이 AI 인프라 투자 확대 및 밸류에이션 매력을 근거로 브로드컴, 팔란티어, 애플 등 대형 기술주를 비롯한 주요 기업들의 투자의견과 목표주가를 대거 상향 조정하며 긍정적인 전망을 제시했습니다. DA데이비슨, “브로드컴, 앤트로픽 자금조달 수혜” 팔란티어 260달러·인텔 140달러 제시 코어위브에는 자금조달 우려 지속 메르카도리브레·퍼거슨 저가매수 의견 월스트리트 표지판 / 로이터 미국 증권사가 브로드컴의 투자의견을 매수로 높이고 팔란티어, 애플의 목표주가를 상향하는 등 대형 기술주에 긍정적인 평가를 이어갔다. AI 기업들의 자금조달과 인프라 투자 확대가 반도체·소프트웨어 기업의 실적을 뒷받침할 것이라는 기대가 투자 판단의 주요 근거로 제시됐다. "실적 발표 전 팔란티어 사라" 27일 CNBC에 따르면 DA데이비슨은 브로드컴을 ‘중립’에서 ‘매수’로 상향했다. 앤트로픽의 기업공개(IPO)가 진행돼 필요한 자본을 조달하고, 내년에는 오픈AI 역시 IPO를 통해 추가 자금을 확보할 가능성이 높다는 판단이다. 이 같은 AI 기업의 자금조달이 브로드컴이 향후 수년간 제시한 성장 기대치를 달성하는 데 도움이 될 것으로 전망했다. 팔란티어에는 높은 밸류에이션에도 강세 전망이 유지됐다. 로젠블랫은 11월 실적 발표를 앞두고 ‘매수’를 재확인하고 목표주가를 225달러에서 260달러로 올렸다. 가치평가 기준 시점을 한 분기 뒤로 이동한 결과로, 1년 뒤 예상 향후 12개월 주당순이익(EPS)의 60배를 적용했다. 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. items.t: Nvidia backs Indian startup helping companies run AI models with fewer GPUs
items.d: Simplismart says its annualized revenue run rate has grown 14-fold in six months, with the U.S. accounting for more than half its revenue.
items.fullText: As the AI boom strains computing capacity, Nvidia has backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million funding round, betting on software that helps companies run AI models more efficiently and, in some cases, with fewer GPUs. Nvidia participated in the all-primary Series B round alongside Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax, with Dallas Venture Capital leading the investment. The deal values the four-year-old startup at about $100 million, including the new funding. Companies are nowadays spending heavily on GPUs to power AI applications, but running those models reliably and economically at scale remains a challenge. Different workloads demand distinct trade-offs between speed, cost, and performance. Deploying and operating AI models to meet business requirements often also requires complex adjustments. Simplismart says its software automates much of that work, tailoring how models run on existing computing infrastructure instead of requiring customers to manage those configurations themselves. “Nobody actually needs the fastest or the cheapest inference,” Amritanshu Jain (pictured above, left), co-founder and CEO of Simplismart, said in an interview. He added that companies instead need to run AI models at speeds and costs that make sense for their specific applications. Simplismart’s software sits between AI models and the computing infrastructure they run on and adjusts how models are deployed and managed to meet customers’ requirements. It says it can optimize factors such as how quickly a model responds, how many requests it handles, and how much computing power it consumes, helping companies get more out of their existing GPU stack. The Bengaluru-based startup offers companies a way to deploy and run AI models through its own platform or within their existing cloud and on-premises infrastructure. SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
items.d: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
items.fullText: SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday . In a statement, SpaceX called the deal the “largest committed GPU financing” . Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, the New York-based private equity giant, will buy the chips and related server hardware, then lease the equipment to SpaceX. The leases will last about five to five-and-a-quarter years, beginning when each tranche of equipment is delivered, according to the filing. SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, subject to closing conditions, with leases starting in the first half of 2027 as the GPUs and related equipment arrive. The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets. “This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans,” SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said in a statement Monday, noting it is seeing “less than one-year payback periods” on its AI infrastructure investments as it scales compute to power Grok and its cloud services. Apollo said the financing will help deliver Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX’s “terrestrial compute buildout.” The financing comes as SpaceX ramps spending to expand its AI infrastructure, alongside its Starlink and launch businesses. The financing follows a blockbuster third quarter for SpaceX’s AI business . SpaceX’s AI segment, which includes the Grok chatbot, the Cursor coding tool, and its cloud compute business, outperformed investor expectations in the third quarter and brought in $7.6 billion of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion in revenue, more than Starlink and rocket launches combined. items.fullText: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations October 21, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster.
